stories.headline: Brazilians vote in presidential runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro
stories.cardLine: Brazilians are voting in a presidential runoff after Flávio Bolsonaro beat incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the first round. Final polls show the race in a statistical dead heat, with Bolsonaro the narrow favorite.

summary.text: Brazilians are voting in a presidential runoff between incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of imprisoned former President Jair Bolsonaro.
The runoff follows an earlier first round in which neither candidate won a majority.
The Guardian reported that Bolsonaro won the first-round vote, a surprise result despite not leading most polls.
Final runoff surveys show the two candidates in a statistical dead heat, according to Newsweek.
The Washington Examiner and International Business Times reported that Bolsonaro, who has President Donald Trump's support, is the slight or narrow favorite.
Bloomberg reported that turnout, public security and the economy are shaping the race, and that Lula is making a last-minute push to mobilize voters through social media.

stories.headline: Starlink service restored in Ukraine as Musk says SpaceX closed a 'loophole'
stories.cardLine: Ukraine says Starlink and Starshield speeds are back to normal after more than a week of disruption. Elon Musk said SpaceX imposed the limits because Ukraine's military used the service for offensive drone strikes, a claim Kyiv disputes.

summary.text: Ukraine's access to the satellite systems Starlink and Starshield was restored to its speeds before the restrictions, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Saturday.
The restoration followed roughly 10 days of throttled connection speeds that disrupted front-line operations.
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said Ukraine's military violated Starlink's terms of service by using the civilian system for offensive drone strikes to kill people.
Musk said in a post on X that the loophole was closed last week, and multiple outlets reported this as an acknowledgment that SpaceX imposed the restrictions.
Ukraine disputes Musk's claim: Serhii Beskrestnov, a defense technology adviser to Zelenskyy, said long-standing restrictions on the civilian system in Ukraine made such offensive use impossible.
Zelenskyy thanked Americans who took the matter seriously, according to Business Insider.
The New York Times reported that drones using Starshield, the Pentagon-funded service, were back to normal speeds.

why.text: Ukraine's military said connectivity to fast-moving military systems was restored after the disruptions.

reading.sentence: More right- than left-leaning coverage

stories.namedOutlets: The New York Times, NBC News, The Wall Street Journal and 18 more

differences.label: Earlier and later reports
differences.text: Musk said Ukraine's military violated Starlink's terms of service by using it for offensive drone strikes; a defense technology adviser to Zelenskyy said long-standing restrictions on the civilian system made such use impossible.

stories.cardLine: A shooting near Florida A&M's Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee injured 12 people, including six children as young as 11, after a fight broke out during homecoming weekend. Five victims have been released from the hospital and one remains critical.

summary.text: Twelve people were injured in a shooting near Florida A&M's Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee on Saturday night during homecoming weekend.
Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence Revell said 11 of the injured suffered gunshot wounds, and six of the victims were children, the youngest 11 years old.
Police said a fight involving two or three individuals broke out shortly before 8 p.m. in a crowded area and led to shots being fired.
Three victims were seriously injured, including one in critical condition, while eight were stable, according to Yahoo News.
Fox News reported that five victims have since been released from the hospital and six remain hospitalized.
Revell said no arrests had been made, and police described the altercation as isolated.
A FAMU student was among the injured, Yahoo News reported.

stories.cardLine: Hundreds of thousands marched across France over school funding and living costs before clashes broke out in Paris. Police fired tear gas and water cannons, and protests also took place in Milan, Rome and Madrid.

summary.text: Hundreds of thousands of people marched across France on Saturday over school funding and soaring living costs, according to multiple outlets.
The demonstrations were largely peaceful before clashes broke out in Paris as a mass march drew to a close.
French police fired tear gas and water cannons on protesters, and shopkeepers boarded up storefronts across Paris.
The Guardian and UPI reported nearly or about 1,000 arrests in France; Breitbart and Newsweek reported more than 1,300.
Breitbart reported the interior ministry said 53 police officers were injured in the clashes.
UPI reported Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said protesters showed up despite bans in several cities.
